_note: What each item weighs, how much room it takes, how many of it go in a slot, and what it takes to unlock it. Transcribed from the MetaForge Wardogs database, which is the same source data/armory.json takes its prices from: every price in this pull matched the price already in the catalogue, which is how the join was checked. Read on 2026-08-31 from a database the site itself dates 2026-08-30, the closed beta build. NOT measured in game, so it carries the same standing as a price: a transcription that a look at the real thing can correct.
_howToRefresh: The API at https://metaforge.app/api/wardogs/database answers a browser and returns 403 to a scripted fetch, so this cannot be a puller script under tools/. Open the site in a browser, fetch that URL from the page, and read weight, gridSize, maxStack, storageGrid, quickSlots, capacity and unlock off each item. Names join exactly except that the six M18 signal grenades carry two spaces after M18 in the source.

_fields.kg: weight, the figure the game puts at the top of the inventory screen
_fields.grid: [width, height] the item takes in a bag, so 1x2 for a rifle magazine
_fields.stack: how many go in one slot before it takes another. Absent means one
_fields.storage: [width, height] a container holds, so 3x5 is 15 slots
_fields.rounds: what a magazine holds, which is also stated in most magazine names
_fields.unlock: the ladder, the level on it, and the one-time cash it costs there
_fields.wip: the source marks the item unfinished and publishes nothing else about it
_fields.class: what the vendor files the weapon under, so a shelf can be split by it
_fields.slot: the attachment slot the vendor files it under, which is the real one rather than a guess from its name
_fields.fits: the weapons it goes on, by name. fitsAny means every weapon with that slot
